name: Chat Emote Bubbles
description: Every emote your chat types floats across your stream in a soap bubble. Type PogChamp five times and five PogChamps drift up and away. Twitch, 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes all count, read straight from Twitch chat with nothing to connect and no bot to add. Ten controls set the look (bubble, snowflake or heart), the speed, the direction, how many can be on screen, where they appear and whether they pop.
changelog: Initial release. The fifth product, and the second that needs nothing beyond the overlay itself.
ready_message: Every emote your chat types is a bubble on your stream right now. The overlay's Controls tab sets the look, the speed and where they appear.
highlights: Every emote your Twitch chat types floats across your stream in a bubble. Five PogChamps in one message are five bubbles.
Three looks: soap bubble, snowflake, heart. Speed, direction, size, color, how many at once, and where they appear.
Nothing to connect and no bot to add. Every change lands in OBS as you make it.

pitch.reasons_heading: Your chat's emotes, on your stream.

reasons.title: Chat sees itself on screen
reasons.body: Every emote someone types turns up on your stream a moment later.

reasons.title: Three looks to start from
reasons.body: Soap bubbles, snowflakes or hearts, in any colour, rising, sinking or fired from one spot.

reasons.title: Nothing to set up
reasons.body: No bot and no account to connect. It reads your Twitch chat directly, like any viewer does.

reasons.title: Keeps going when we don't
reasons.body: Emotes come straight from Twitch, not through Overlabels, so the bubbles keep coming even if Overlabels has a bad day.

pitch.looks_lede: Pick one in the designer, then change the colour, size, speed and direction to suit your stream.
pitch.setup_note: Size the browser source to your whole canvas, 1920 by 1080, and put it above your camera.

faq.a: Twitch emotes, plus the 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes enabled in your channel. A plain emoji is text, not an emote, so it stays in chat.

faq.q: Can a busy chat flood my screen?
faq.a: No. You set how many bubbles can be on screen at once, 40 by default.

faq.q: Do my viewers need to do anything?
faq.a: No. They chat like they always do.

pitch.closing: Let your chat's emotes loose tonight.

notes: Every emote comes from Twitch directly, over the same public connection any chat viewer uses. Nothing passes through Overlabels, so the bubbles keep coming even when Overlabels is having a bad day.

Size the OBS browser source to your whole canvas (1920 by 1080) and put it above your camera. Bubbles rise from the bottom edge by default; the Spawn control moves them to the top, to a random spot, or to one point you pick with X and Y.
Pop after is 0 by default, so bubbles float off the top of the screen. Set it to a number of seconds and they gather at the edge and pop after that long instead.
Only pictures are bubbled: Twitch emotes and the 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes enabled in your channel. A plain emoji like a party popper is text, not an emote, and stays in chat.
